summary.text: 馆 means a public building or institution. It is the simplified form of 館, traditionally analyzed as a compound with 食 marking a food-related category and 官 supplying the sound. The older gloss “guest lodging” is also recorded.

formation.text: The traditional analysis of 館 is phonosemantic: 食 contributes a food-related meaning category, and 官 provides a sound cue. In 馆, 饣 is the conventional side form corresponding to 食. An earlier use of 宛 for the lodging word is reported, but how it relates to the 食+官 analysis remains unresolved.

components.text: 饣 is the simplified side form corresponding to 食, the food-related meaning element in the traditional analysis of 館. The evidence identifies 馆 as simplified from 館 but does not date this spelling in the character.

官 is the phonetic element in the traditional analysis of 館. In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 官 is reconstructed as /*kʷˤa[n]/ and 館 as *[k]ˤo[n]ʔ-s, a broad historical sound relationship. The proposed sound merger and replacement of 宛 by 官 remain uncertain.

sound_limitation.text: The cited sound comparison supports a broad historical relationship, but the specific proposed sound merger and replacement pathway is a secondary account and is not independently verified.

sound.text: The Old Chinese reconstructions differ in detail but indicate a broad historical sound relationship; modern Mandarin readings alone do not establish it.

history.text: The seal-script-style redraw illustrates traditional 館 with 食 on the left and 官 on the right, matching the traditional dictionary analysis. It is a modern redraw, not an artifact image, and does not show a sequence from 宛 to 館.
馆 is identified as the simplified form of 館; the date when 饣 was standardized in this character is not given.
A secondary proposal gives an earlier form 𩜌 with 食 and 宛, followed by 官 replacing 宛 as the phonetic element after a sound merger. This proposed graphic and sound sequence remains uncertain.
舘 is recorded as a nonstandard variant associated with lodging and the use of 舍; it is not established as an ancestor of 館.

uncertainties.text: Oracle-bone and bronze uses of 宛 for the lodging word are reported, but the individual inscriptions lack securely established dates and independently verified artifact images. Their relationship to 館’s 食+官 analysis is unresolved.
The proposed sound history linking 官 and 館 uses system-specific reconstructions. The precise sound change and its role in replacing 宛 remain unverified.

senses.text: A traditional dictionary glosses 館 as lodging for guests and quotes a description of route stations holding provisions for visitors. The earliest securely dated attestation is unresolved.
馆 is used for public buildings and institutions. The available examples do not establish when or by what sequence this broader use developed from the lodging sense.

developments.text: Both lodging and public-building senses are recorded, but a dated transition between them is not established.

limitations.text: The reported early use of 宛 is a graph used for the lodging word; it does not show that another word’s meaning changed into “lodging.” Individual inscriptions are not securely dated or independently verified.
Recorded uses include residences, institutions, teaching venues, and service establishments, but their chronology and any continuous semantic development are not established.

overview.text: 馆 means a public building or institution. It is simplified from 館, whose traditional analysis pairs a food-related element with a sound element; an older recorded sense is “guest lodging.”

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, via Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry reads 館, “guest lodging”; it analyzes the graph as 食 plus 官 as phonetic, and quotes the Zhouli about a 館 along the route with stored supplies for visiting diplomatic guests. This is a historical dictionary account, not independent proof of the graph’s earliest formation.
evidence.title: [A04602] 館 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry records 舘 as a variant and explains it as a popular spelling using 舍, associated with the lodging sense. Its shape should be treated as a nonstandard variant, not an established ancestor of 館. The cited entry includes a Shuowen seal form and references later character dictionaries, but says its ancient-script chart is not publicly available.
evidence.title: [A04602] 館 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The database states that oracle-bone examples of 宛, graphically composed of 宀 and 夗, were read as 館 and meant lodging; it also reports a bronze inscription reading 仲義父作新宛(館)寶鼎. The source supplies the reading and lodging use, while its displayed text does not give a secure date for these individual inscriptions. This is evidence for an earlier graph used for the lodging word, distinct from the later 食+官 phonetic compound analysis.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析: 宀

evidence.text: The database analyzes early 官 as 宀 plus 𠂤, describing 𠂤 as an archaic 師 and interpreting the whole as people or officials meeting under a roof. It reports oracle-bone use as a place-name and bronze uses for an office/administrative place, administration, and office/position. It also records a separate proposal that 官 was the original graph for 館, depicting a group resting in a lodging; that is a distinct analysis and does not itself show that 官 is the phonetic element in 館.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析: 宀

evidence.source: Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin guān and lists senses including official, office or post, and an administrative office or residence. It reproduces the Shuowen analysis of 官 separately from 館. This supports the component’s independent word and reading but does not establish its pronunciation in every earlier stage by itself.
evidence.title: A01015 官 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

These reconstructions are in the source’s Old Chinese framework and indicate a historical sound relationship, though the page is secondary and the particular sound-change account is not independently demonstrated by the other inspected sources.

evidence.text: This secondary account proposes that 宛 was first used for the lodging word, that 食 was added to form 𩜌, and that 官 later replaced 宛 as phonetic after a sound merger. The inspected primary sources do not independently establish this full sequence; it remains a cited proposal.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.

search_audit.outcome: Oracle, bronze, and big-seal file opens failed (internal errors/cache miss). Their identity and reuse provenance were not established, so they were not selected. The Commons 館-seal page was inspected successfully.

gaps: No dated primary image or independently inspected inscription for the reported 宛/館 oracle-bone and bronze examples was available in this research pass; the CUHK database text supports the reported reading/use but the exact inscription chronology remains unverified here.

The earliest dated attestation of the lodging sense is not established by the consulted pages. Shuowen and its Zhouli quotation preserve an early lexical account, but a dictionary gloss sequence is not a chronology of semantic development.
The semantic progression from guest lodging to broader public buildings or institutions is plausible from usage, but no dated sequence establishing when each extension arose was verified.

The distinct phonetic analysis 食+官 is supported by Shuowen and modern dictionary descriptions. A separate proposal treats 官 as the original graph for 館; these should not be conflated. The evidence consulted does not settle the relation of that proposal to the attested 宛 writing.

The specific sound-change explanation for replacement of 宛 by 官 as phonetic is available here through a secondary page citing Baxter; it was not checked against the cited book directly. Modern 官 guān and 館 guǎn differ in tone, and no inference about phonetic function should rely only on modern readings.
The simplified form 馆 is identified as simplified 館, but the consulted sources do not provide a dated standardization record for the change 食 to 饣.

CUHK’s displayed 官 analysis reports multiple early uses, including a place-name, but it does not establish whether a separate early reading for the lodging word can be securely reconstructed from those usages.
No whole-graph borrowing claim is proposed for 館, so no source-word/object-name borrowing investigation applies.

The earliest securely dated inscription for the lodging word remains unestablished. CUHK reports oracle-bone and bronze uses of 宛 for 館 but the inscription date, artifact image, and reading were not independently checked against a primary publication.

The link between lodging and later meanings such as institutions, restaurants, schools, and museums is not demonstrated as a dated semantic chain. Dictionary examples are evidence for uses, not proof of their relative chronology.

Shuowen's 食+官 analysis supports the traditional compound analysis, but does not settle how it relates to the earlier 宛 spelling reported by CUHK. A separate proposal says 𩜌 preceded 館 and 官 replaced 宛 after a sound merger; the detailed reconstruction has not been checked directly against Baxter or the cited paleographic monographs.

官 has modern Mandarin guān and 館 has guǎn; modern readings alone do not establish the historical phonetic relation. The cited Old Chinese comparisons are framework-specific secondary data; the proposed exact merger and replacement pathway remains insufficiently verified.

The target is simplified 馆, while the best-established component analysis is for traditional 館. Available sources identify 馆 as its simplified counterpart but do not date the standardization of 饣 in this character.
No sound borrowing of a whole graph is proposed. No depicted object or recoverable object-name borrowing claim was found.
